Experience Strategist (also known as CX or UX strategist, CRM strategist)
The CX strategist is a problem-solving thinker delivering business insights through understanding audiences, developing data-led decisions, customer experiences and strategy direction. Day-to-day they concentrate on guiding strategy across key accounts while delivering industry-leading service, which includes: Analyzing a variety of data-centric resources, hacking data, researching behaviours, looking at what people are doing and hypothesizing why. Micro-journey planning:  documenting workshops and creating design artefacts such as storyboards, as-is and future-state journey flows to help clients understand the best solution for the customer.

Experience Designer (also known as UX or UI Designer)

UI/UX Designer responsibilities include gathering requirements, creative design (including some print) and wireframing. To be successful in this role, you should have experience as a UI/UX Designer or a similar role. Responsibilities & skills: Gather and evaluate user requirements, Effectively communicate design ideas using a variety of methods including but not limited to wireframes, sketches and flow diagrams, Present and communicate effectively with our clients, Identify and troubleshoot UX problems, Up-to-date knowledge of relevant design software, Strong communication skills to collaborate with various stakeholders
Salary – Over threshold 

All of the above roles require a relevant tertiary qualification or a minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in lieu of qualification.
Roles could also be available in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane

Data Communications Technician | Brisbane Based | Travel Across QLD | Full-Time Opportunity   Your new company     HAYS has partnered with a well-established and growing communications specialist delivering fibre optic solutions across Queensland. With a strong pipeline of work and a reputation for quality and safety, this organisation prides itself on developing its people and investing in long-term careers.    Your new role     As a Data Communications Technician, you will be working across a mix of local Brisbane sites and remote Queensland projects, installing and maintaining fibre optic communication systems.    This is a hands-on role suited to someone who enjoys variety, problem-solving, and working in dynamic environments.   This role involves regular work at heights (6-10 meter transmission structures) and in confined spaces. You must be comfortable working at heights, as this is an essential requirement of the position.    Your day-to-day responsibilities will include: 
 
 Installing, maintaining, and troubleshooting fibre optic and data communication systems 
 Conducting site surveys to assess and deliver tailored communication solutions 
 Reading and interpreting cable plans and technical drawings 
 Performing high-quality installations in line with industry standards 
 Working at heights and within confined spaces in a safe and controlled manner 
 Liaising with clients to understand requirements and deliver effective outcomes 
 Ensuring all work is completed safely, efficiently, and to specification 
 
  What you'll need to succeed     We are open-minded on background - the key focus for us is attitude, aptitude, and a genuine interest in data communications.   You'll ideally bring: 
 
 Experience in telecommunications, electrical, or data communications environments 
 Exposure to fibre optic installation, termination, or testing (highly regarded) 
 ACMA Open Cabling Registration (or willingness to obtain) 
 Current manual driver's licence 
 Ability to work autonomously and as part of a team 
 Strong problem-solving skills and a safety-first mindset 
 Flexibility to travel to remote sites (Monday-Friday) 
  Comfort and capability working at heights (essential)  
 A proactive attitude and willingness to learn and develop 
 
  Desirable but not essential:  
 
 Cert III in Telecommunications 
 MR Licence (or willingness to obtain - support provided) 
 Previous site-based experience in infrastructure, electrical, or comms projects 
 
  What you'll get in return     
 
 Stable, full-time employment with a strong project pipeline   
 Opportunity to work across diverse sites throughout Queensland (home on weekends)   
 Flights, transport, and logistics provided for remote work   
 Ongoing training, mentoring, and career development pathways   
 A supportive team culture that values attitude and effort   
 Competitive salary package   
 
  What you need to do now     If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV to jarred.ware@hays.com.au, or call us now on 3243 3021.   If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.    Please  click here  to apply.

result.description:
For nearly 25 years, APD Global has set the benchmark in delivering advanced, comprehensive, and specialised engineering solutions.

We have around 800 employees including our alliance contracting partners, across 15 strategically located offices in Australia (Perth, Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide, Darwin), New Zealand and Malaysia. We specialise in seamless integration across the Power Systems, Telecommunications, and Renewable Energy industries. Our expertise spans Power Systems Studies, Transmission Lines, Substations, Telecommunications, Protection, Control & Automation, Renewable Energy Connections, Mining, and Engineering, Protection Panel Design and Installation, 3D Design and Manufacturing as well as Construction/Management (EPC/M) services.

We have outstanding opportunity for a highly experienced ACCEPTANCE ENGINEER. We are looking for trustworthy individuals with integrity who will bring a positive can-do attitude to the position and to the team. Position available in Vic, Qld, WA, and NSW.

Role Overview
The Acceptance Engineer works under the direction of the Acceptance Lead to support the successful acceptance, handover, and integration of new and upgraded network assets into Telstra’s operational environment. The role is responsible for ensuring all documentation, as-built records, and asset data are accurate, compliant, and correctly uploaded into Telstra’s DBoR systems in accordance with program and governance requirements.

KEY RESPONSIBILITY

ACCEPTANCE & HANDOVER
Support the Acceptance Lead in managing the end-to-end acceptance process for Telstra network assets.
Review and validate construction completion packs, ensuring readiness for acceptance and operational handover.
Facilitate the smooth transition of assets from delivery teams into Telstra operational ownership.

DOCUMENTATION & AS-BUILTS
Ensure all project documentation, including as-built drawings, design updates, and asset data, is accurate, complete, and compliant.
Upload and validate as-built information within Telstra’s DBoR systems upon project completion.
Maintain document version control and ensure alignment between physical assets and system records.

DBoR SYSTEM MANAGEMENT
Create, update, and validate asset records using Telstra’s legacy and current DBoR platforms, including: IDEAL, CANRAD, Structure Builder, MITS, RODS, RFNSA, CADlink, Multiman, CRAMER, TPD, WHISPER, TCSS, NETMAPS, WidePlan, Widefeas, CMART, and TRAC.
Resolve data discrepancies and support data quality audits as required by the program.

STAKEHOLDER COORDINATION
Work closely with the Acceptance Lead, internal Telstra teams, delivery partners, and external contractors to coordinate acceptance activities.
Support issue resolution relating to site access, design compliance, documentation gaps, and system data conflicts.
Act as a key interface between construction, design, and operational teams during acceptance and handover.

COMPLIANCE & GOVERNANCE
Ensure all works comply with Telstra design guidelines, relevant Australian Standards, and WHS/safety requirements.
Support program governance by ensuring acceptance processes align with Telstra policies and audit requirements.
Assist with continuous improvement initiatives across acceptance and handover processes.

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE/QUALIFICATIONS
Experience working in network acceptance, handover, or asset management roles within Telstra or similar telecommunications environments.
Strong working knowledge of Telstra DBoR systems and acceptance workflows.
Ability to interpret engineering designs, construction drawings, and as-built documentation.
Strong stakeholder management and coordination skills.
High attention to detail with a focus on data accuracy and compliance.

If you have the skills required for this role and you feel this is the job for you, then apply now!
Work Location: Melbourne, Vic
Salary: $80,000 per annum + Super
